finding.claim: Default SCP remote-path quoting escapes only double quotes, so attacker-influenced path strings passed to ScpClient methods can inject shell commands on the remote SSH host (CWE-78).
finding.source: Remote path/filename string passed by the application to ScpClient public methods (Upload/Download overloads, ScpClient.cs:349-580), when derived from untrusted input.
finding.sink: SendExecRequest exec command built at ScpClient.cs:367, 410, 459, 498, 538, 578 and run by the remote POSIX shell (ChannelSession.cs:197).

trace.note: Upload(FileInfo, path) accepts the remote path.
path passed through _remotePathTransformation.Transform(posixPath.Directory) into scp -t command.
DefaultTransform returns RemotePathTransformation.DoubleQuote; used by convenience constructors at ScpClient.cs:270-298.
Wraps path in double quotes and escapes only '"' (lines 61-63); '$', backtick and '\' are left unescaped.
Download(filename, Stream) builds string.Concat("scp -f ", Transform(filename)) and sends it as an exec request.
SendExecRequest sends the command string to the remote SSH server for shell execution.

finding.guards_checked: Only control on path is the double-quote escape at RemotePathDoubleQuoteTransformation.cs:61-63 (enforced but incomplete). Shell-quote alternative RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation exists but is opt-in only (RemotePathTransformation.cs:82-84); not fully verified. No allowlist or other sanitizer on the path.

finding.claim: ForwardedPortDynamic(uint port) binds its unauthenticated SOCKS listener to all interfaces (IPAddress.Any), letting any network peer use the client host as an open proxy into the SSH server's network (CWE-1188/CWE-284; conditional on the app starting this forward).
finding.source: Any network peer that can reach the client's listening port, sending a SOCKS4/5 request.
finding.sink: Listener bound at ForwardedPortDynamic.cs:157-166; SOCKS requests open direct-tcpip channels to attacker-chosen hosts (ForwardedPortDynamic.cs:327-334, 546-563).

trace.note: InternalStart sets ip = IPAddress.Any when BoundHost is empty.
SOCKS client requiring authentication is rejected; no-auth clients are accepted, so the proxy is unauthenticated.
Contrast: ForwardedPortLocal resolves a required BoundHost and has no wildcard default.

finding.guards_checked: No bind-address restriction and no client authentication on the dynamic forward. Could be an intentional library default, so severity is conditional on app usage.
